chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hajjal, from Dawud ibn Farqad and Ali ibn Uqba and Tha'laba, raised it to Abu Abdillah and Abu Ja'far, or one of them (peace be upon him), who said:
Frequent joking removes the water (dignity) of the face, and frequent laughter hurls out faith with a hurling.

key_terms.مَاءِ الْوَجْهِ: Water of the face (metaphor for dignity, presence, or luster)
key_terms.مَجّاً: With a hurling or casting out

ai.seo_question: What is the effect of excessive laughter and joking on faith and dignity in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (or Imam al-Baqir), linking the physical expression of 'water of the face' (dignity and composure) to the spiritual state of the heart. Scholars interpret 'expelling faith' not as total loss of belief, but as a weakening of its presence and vitality, warning that frivolity distracts the heart from divine remembrance. This serves as a practical ethical guideline for maintaining khushu' (humility) and presence of mind in daily interactions.
